material_selection_reason: NOT a material-preference claim. This stage qualifies on Volume exactly as the approved plan predicted: it reads apps/web/src/routes/admin.tsx, the owner shell, two existing owner section subtrees in full, the hook-and-messages pattern, the admin.access procedure surface, the browser-spec auth and screenshot conventions, and returns a one-page map. scripts/resolve-opencode-worker.mjs was run on a stage input recorded before any of this stage's own target-file reading, with zero delegation-lifecycle violations, and it reduced the pool to exactly two fully qualified external candidates - deepseek-v4-pro and glm-5.3 - between which NO material stage-specific evidence advantage exists in either direction. The selection between those two is a neutral tie resolution, not a capability judgement. See tie_resolution.

tie_resolution.basis: human routing instruction of 2026-08-24 for this run: a tie between two or more fully qualified external candidates is not a reason to fall back to a native subagent. Where the workflow filters leave several externals materially tied, the winner stays inside the tied qualified external set and is chosen deterministically. Native remains available only where every external route is disqualified by a material workflow constraint, never merely tied.
tie_resolution.rule: deterministic lexicographic ascending order of candidate_id over the tied eligible set
evidence_considered_and_rejected_as_sepa: deepseek-v4-pro has 5 recorded outcome_history entries and glm-5.3 has 0. Absence of recorded outcomes is absence of evidence, not evidence of a disadvantage, and treating it as a separator would manufacture a capability advantage the evidence does not support.

the deepseek-v4-pro entry of 2026-08-23T12:50 is ESCALATED. Escalation is the return contract working as designed, not a gate failure, and it is followed by three PASS entries. It is not a separator against that candidate either.

long_structured_return_assessment: long_structured_return_is_material IS declared here, and this is the deliberate difference from the p11_browser_debt_b01 stage-1 decision, which considered the same flag and declined it. That stage returned a four-row map on ONE axis - one mechanism and one proposed wait per location. This stage acceptance depends on five structurally distinct topics arriving in one message (owner-section mount and shell contribution; the messages.ts plus use-*-messages.ts plus hook composition; the admin.access procedure surface; browser-spec owner authentication and /admin driving; canonical screenshot naming and scoping) PLUS an enumeration whose completeness is itself load-bearing. The approved plan names refusal-to-copy incompleteness as a defect class equivalent to M1: a refusal with no copy path surfaces to the owner as a bare error. A truncated return here does not merely cost a re-run, it can silently ship an incomplete inventory into stage 3. Declaring the flag is the fail-closed reading. The selected candidate carries no constraint against this flag; it filters ox-alpha only.
